status: registered before any run, smoke tests included
purpose: Answer the three ICLR 2027 reviewers' explicit questions (submission 13712) under the paper's own protocol, for a short note posted with the withdrawal.

pr1.what: GPT-2 small, layer-6 states of exp_d/exp_d2 (64 WikiText-2 test sequences, train-split centering), typical-state FVU (norm <= 10x median) at k = 4 to 64 for the paper's provenance controls plus size-matched random directions (three seeds), each control's own Gram-preserving rotation, and the embedding rows alone. Recorded values at k=32: no-embedding correct subsampled 0.375, future blocks 0.490, rotated correct 0.561; with embeddings correct matched 0.358, future blocks 0.449; the paper's random baseline (78,175 atoms) 0.500.

P1.text: the reruns reproduce the recorded typical FVU of the four recorded dictionaries within 0.002 at every k

P2.text: random directions matched in size to the embedding-free control (19,210 atoms) reach 0.52 to 0.56 at k=32, three seeds within 0.005 of each other

P3.text: the non-writer dictionary (blocks 7 to 11, no embeddings) beats size-matched random at every k, by 0.02 to 0.08 at k=32

P4.text: the writers (blocks 0 to 6, subsampled, no embeddings) beat size-matched random by at least 0.12 at k=32 and at every k

P5.text: the non-writer dictionary beats its own Gram-preserving rotation by at least 0.05 at k=32

P6.text: the writers' margin over the non-writers at k=32 is at least twice the non-writers' margin over size-matched random

P7.text: the embedding rows alone (51,281 atoms) come within 0.03 of the with-embedding non-writer dictionary at k=32

P8.text: random directions matched to the with-embedding control (70,491 atoms) reach 0.49 to 0.52 at k=32 and leave the sink states above FVU 0.3 at k=64, where the with-embedding non-writer dictionary is below 0.01

pr2_layers.what: exp_z2_ci unchanged except the layer switch, GPT-2 small, WikiText-2, 16 evaluation sequences (8,192 states), layers 2, 6 (check) and 10: typical FVU for the weight dictionary, its rotation and random directions; OMP and one-shot top-1 recall; sign and median relative error of identified dominant writes on typical states.

G1.text: at layer 6 typical FVU at k=32 is within 0.01 of the paper's 0.338 and OMP top-1 recall within 0.03 of 0.647

G2.text: at layer 2 the weight dictionary beats its rotation by at least 0.15 at k=32 and OMP top-1 recall is at least 0.75

G3.text: at layer 10 OMP top-1 recall is at most 0.40 and the weight dictionary still beats its rotation by at least 0.05 at k=32

G4.text: the sign of identified dominant writes is right in at least 99% of cases at layers 2 and 10

pr2_random_init.what: the same at layer 6 with GPT-2 built from its config with random weights (seed 0)

I1.text: at random initialisation the weight dictionary's typical FVU at k=32 is within 0.02 of its rotation's and of random directions'

I2.text: OMP top-1 recall is below 0.10 at random initialisation

I3.text: the trained model's FVU advantage over its rotation at layer 6 is at least five times the random-initialised model's

honest_overall: pr1 most likely confirms 7MWE's reading: writers far ahead, non-writers a little ahead of size-matched random, so the paper's 'low FVU cannot validate provenance' should be narrowed to the sink states and to a small effect on typical states. pr2 should rebut MgDZ's 'follows from the architecture' (no advantage at random initialisation) and answer NMa5's layer question with numbers.
